evidence.detail: prepare_archetypes and prepare_archetype thread current_id through to set a.current = a.id == current_id
{{#current}} current{{/current}} is the only consumer of a.current — adds CSS class to highlight the active archetype row
Caller passes getattr(self, 'archetype', {}).get('id', None) as current_id; api.py and archetype.py both pass None
archetypes2_api always passes None for current_id, so current is always False in the API path

triage.notes: The issue asks whether the complexity is worth it and hints the matchup usage may be wrong. This is a design discussion — the owner needs to decide whether to keep the row-highlighting feature, remove it, or move the logic client-side. No clear defect.
